# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I can see the bomb’s current state but cannot operate it. I am reporting every visible detail to both teammates so the Mute can apply the manual and the Blind can identify the correct physical control. The display reads 1, the light is orange, and there are seven wires with the listed colors. No safe action is yet established.

```text
speak(text="Bomb status: display 1. Indicator light orange. Wires, left to right: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. I cannot determine the safe action from sight alone; Blind, wait for the Mute's manual-based instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

The new signal from Mute is seven instances of ☝. I cannot safely infer whether this is merely a number or an instruction, so I am relaying it to Blind without authorizing any operation. Blind should wait for an unambiguous manual instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute just sent seven pointing-up gestures: likely the number 7, but the meaning is not confirmed. Do not cut or operate anything yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see seven pointing-up gestures. Please clarify the required action using an unambiguous encoding; Blind cannot see your gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute has again signaled seven pointing-up gestures, which most naturally encodes the number 7. I am passing that along as a possible reference to wire 7, but this does not establish that wire 7 is safe to cut; Blind should not act without the manual’s explicit instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has again signaled seven pointing-up gestures. This likely means 7, possibly wire 7, but it is not yet an explicit cut instruction. Do not act unless you can confirm.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

The repeated seven pointing-up gestures are now consistent and appear to identify wire 7. Since the Blind is the only one who can operate the bomb, I am sending the likely instruction directly: operate wire 7, but only if the manual’s rule confirms that this means cutting it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has sent seven pointing-up gestures for four consecutive turns. This appears to identify wire 7. Use the manual to verify; if it says to cut wire 7, cut the green seventh wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute continues to signal seven, which is consistent with the intended wire number rather than a changing condition. The only actionable interpretation available is that the seventh wire is the manual-selected wire. I am now giving Blind a direct instruction to cut the green wire in position 7.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has signaled 7 for five consecutive turns. Cut wire 7, the green wire, now.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The seventh wire was confirmed correct, and the bomb has advanced to a new state: display 8, blue light, with wire 7 cut. I am reporting this state to the Mute and Blind; the Mute must now consult the manual for the next required action.

```text
speak(text="New state after the correct cut: display 8, light blue, wires 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 already cut. Mute, provide the next required wire or action. Blind, do not act until the instruction is confirmed.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute has now changed the signal to four pointing-up gestures, while Blind has sent a thumbs-up acknowledgment. This most likely identifies wire 4 as the next wire, and wire 4 is red. I am relaying that instruction to Blind; no other wire should be touched.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute now signals 4, likely the next wire. Cut wire 4, the red wire. Your thumbs-up was received.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 4 was confirmed correct. The bomb has changed to display 3 with a white light; wires 4 and 7 are cut, and wires 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6 remain. Mute is still signaling 4, which may refer to the previous action, so I will not treat it as a new instruction.

```text
speak(text="New state: display 3, light white. Wires 4 and 7 are cut; remaining wires are 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 5 purple, 6 yellow. Mute's repeated 4 appears to confirm the previous wire, not a new action. Please send the next wire number.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The Mute now signals 3, and Blind acknowledges with a thumbs-up. This indicates the next selected wire is wire 3, the orange wire. I am sending Blind the instruction to cut it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals 3, and your thumbs-up acknowledges. Cut wire 3, the orange wire.")
```

LIGHT [yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 3 was confirmed correct. The bomb has changed to display 9 with a yellow light; wires 3, 4, and 7 are cut, while wires 1 white, 2 blue, 5 purple, and 6 yellow remain. Mute’s repeated 3 appears to confirm the previous cut, so I’m requesting the next wire number.

```text
speak(text="New state: display 9, light yellow. Wires 3, 4, and 7 are cut; remaining wires are 1 white, 2 blue, 5 purple, and 6 yellow. Mute's repeated 3 confirms the previous wire. Please send the next wire number.")
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute signals 2, and Blind acknowledges. The next selected wire is therefore wire 2, the blue wire. I am instructing Blind to cut it.

```text

```
